In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of environmental factors on cancer, and the aim of our studies is to reduce the incidence of cancer by identifying and modifying the causes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of cancer can be greatly reduced by the avoidance of tobacco, alcohol, and ionizing radiation.
the incidence of cancer in the industrialized world can be reduced by at least 80%.
80% of all fatal cancers could be avoided by a combination of changes in behaviour and environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk of cancer in middle or old age could be reduced by about 80% if all the avoidable risks were eliminated.
40% of fatal cancer cases could be avoided if all avoidable risk factors were eliminated.
, with the exception of smoking, we have not yet found the most effective way of reducing cancer mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be able to reduce the incidence of fatal cancers in Germany by 50% by the year 2000 if all the avoidable factors are taken into account.

the incidence of cancer in the population as a whole can be reduced by 70%-80% if all the avoidable factors are eliminated, although this would require a major change in the lifestyle of the population.

the proportion of cancers attributable to environmental and lifestyle factors is very high, so that the incidence of cancer can be reduced by 60%-80% and the mortality by 50%-80% if the factors are avoided.
